The Library is unfiltered and complete, while observer-relative coherence determines which continuations remain accessible to a particular observer. When stable transitions recur across an appropriate family of surviving paths, the recurrence can be described as regularity without being promoted to a primitive law.

Law-like regularity therefore cannot be inserted as a primitive rule without changing the dependency structure of the framework.

Instead, the framework distinguishes between the existence of candidate continuations within the complete Library and the observer-relative ability to maintain those continuations as coherent traversal. The unfiltered continuation space contains the candidate paths; survivorship restricts that space according to the observer's coherence relation.

content.title: Unfiltered continuation space
content.text: For x ∈ 𝓜, define Ω(x) as the subset of the complete path space whose paths begin at x.
content.interpretation: Ω(x) is not a generated future or a local ontological neighborhood. It is a reference-indexed subset of an already-complete relational path structure.

content.text: Because 𝓜 is static and maximally complete, selecting x as a current relational reference does not cause a new region of the Library to come into existence. The reference simply determines which represented paths count as continuations from that position.

When an observer O has an accumulated history h ending at x, continuation is further restricted by observer-relative coherence. The appropriate condition is therefore expressed directly through 𝓒(γ | O,h,x) = 1. The previously used γ_noise threshold is eliminated at the foundational level because coherence is already defined through the observer-specific resolution floor I_N(O).

content.title: Observer-relative coherent continuation
content.text: The coherent continuation space consists of paths extending h from x that remain coherent relative to O.
content.interpretation: Γ_O(h,x) is a relational filtering of the complete path space. It does not constitute a second ontology and does not replace Ω(x).

content.text: The distinction is therefore between candidate paths represented in the totality and paths that can remain coherently traversable for a particular observer. A path may belong to Ω(x) while failing to belong to Γ_O(h,x). Such failure does not remove the path from Path(𝓜), nor does it remove any of its configurations from 𝓜.

content.title: Continuation inclusion
content.text: Observer-relative coherent continuation is a restricted subset of the unfiltered continuation space.

This construction also preserves the absence of a privileged origin. Any admissible x ∈ 𝓜 may serve as the observer's current relational reference. If coherent continuation existed only from a distinguished configuration, that configuration would acquire the status of a privileged universal origin, contradicting the reference-frame neutrality of the Library.

content.title: Nonempty coherent continuation
content.text: Under the combined NSFG assumptions, every admissible observer-relative reference configuration admits at least one coherent continuation.
content.interpretation: This is a derived structural requirement of the combined framework. It is not claimed to follow from maximal completeness alone.

content.text: The requirement is stronger than merely asserting that every x belongs to the Library. Library membership guarantees inclusion in the static totality; coherent continuation additionally requires that the observer's present state, history, resolution, and magnitude evaluation admit at least one maintainable path. The distinction between these statements is essential.
The Library therefore remains invariant under traversal. The observer's accessible relation may change as the reference and history change, but the underlying totality does not.

content.title: Library invariance under traversal
content.text: Traversal changes the observer-relative relation to the Library rather than the Library itself.
content.interpretation: There is no temporal generation of successive Libraries. The index i represents an abstract traversal ordering and is not, by itself, physical time.

content.text: Survivorship can now be understood as a filtering relation rather than an ontological deletion mechanism. The paths outside Γ_O(h,x) remain part of the complete continuation structure even though they are not maintained as coherent traversal by O.

When particular transitions recur across an appropriate family of observer-accessible surviving paths, that recurrence may be described as a regularity. Such regularity is downstream of distinction, resolution, distinguishability, coherence, and survivorship. It therefore need not be inserted as an independent axiom.

content.title: Observer-relative emergent regularity
content.text: Let L_O(x,y) denote a derived relation in which the transition x → y is stable and recurring across an appropriate family of O-accessible paths.
content.latex: L_O(x,y) = 1 \iff x \to y \text{ is a stable recurring transition across an appropriate family of O-accessible paths}
content.interpretation: L_O describes regularity emerging from repeated survivorship. It does not impose a governing law upon the Library.

content.text: The resulting dependency is therefore asymmetric: the axiomatic distinction generates the formal structures from which observer-relative coherence can be defined; coherent survivorship restricts accessible continuation; repeated structure among those survivors can then be described as law-like regularity. The regularity is an observed consequence of the filtering structure, not a premise of it.
The whole road is already there; the reference determines which road can be walked.

The road represents the complete path structure Path(𝓜). Choosing x as the current relational reference identifies which paths count as continuations, while observer-relative coherence determines which of those paths can remain traversable. The observer changes its relation to the whole rather than causing the whole to become.

content.text: Consider a family of paths evaluated relative to an observer O, its relevant history h, and current reference configuration x. These paths are drawn from the unchanged total path domain Path(𝓜). A transition that repeatedly survives observer-relative coherence across an appropriate family of such paths can exhibit stable recurrence relative to O.

Survivorship therefore operates on traversal relations, not on the ontology of the Library. A transition may fail to remain coherent for observer O without the configurations or candidate paths involved thereby being removed from 𝓜 or from the total path domain. The incoherent complement remains represented in the Library; only its continuation through the observer-maintained coherent relation is not retained as part of that traversal.

It can support a derived description of stable regularity.
It does not add a governing rule to the axiomatic floor.

It does not establish that the observed recurrence is universal or observer-independent.

content.text: The important distinction is between requiring a transition and observing that a transition repeatedly survives. The former would introduce a governing rule into the axiomatic floor; the latter is a descriptive identification of a stable pattern within the relational structure produced by observer-relative coherence.

Thus, a transition does not become regular because an external law commands it to occur. It becomes law-like when its recurrence is stable across an appropriate observer-accessible ensemble. Such regularity is therefore derived from repeated survivorship rather than imposed upon the Library.

Survivorship is the mechanism by which domain-specific regularities emerge from the domain-neutral foundation. In physical contexts, survivorship corresponds to the persistence of physical laws across observations; in AI contexts, to the stability of symbolic patterns across reasoning steps; in financial contexts, to the recurrence of market trends across trading periods. The structural mechanism is the same in all domains.

The existence of at least one coherent continuation from an admissible reference configuration is a separate structural requirement of the model. It does not imply that every candidate continuation survives, nor does it follow from recurrence itself. Survivorship may restrict the observer's experienced continuation relation while leaving the complete Library unchanged.

The relevant regularity remains relational: it is regularity as established within the observer's accessible and resolution-maintained traversal structure, not necessarily an observer-independent law imposed upon the entire Library. The totality remains maximally complete regardless of which transitions survive for a particular observer.

section.title: Why Navigation Becomes Inevitable
section.purpose: Bridge the foundational ontology into NSFG's central problem of coherent navigation. Once the Library is defined as an unfiltered configuration space and observer-relative coherence restricts which transitions remain resolvable, continuation becomes a constrained traversal problem over an already-existing totality.

section.cipher_explanation: Persistent distinction requires transitions that remain resolvable to the observer. Because coherence is observer-relative, the set of continuations that can sustain persistence may be narrower than the full set of paths represented in the Library. Navigation therefore emerges as the problem of continuing through the observer-relative coherent subset without implying that the Library itself changes or generates a future.

content.text: Where distinction persists, continuation narrows. Where continuation narrows, a path must be followed.

Navigation does not enter the framework as a new primitive. It appears because persistence creates a continuation problem. The Library \mathcal{M} is an unchanged, unfiltered totality containing the configurations and paths under consideration. Observer-relative coherence then determines which transitions can remain distinguishable to a particular observer O. The resulting accessible continuation space may therefore be narrower than the total path space even though the underlying Library remains unchanged.

The road is one; the travelers are many. Navigation is the continuation problem that all domains share. In physical contexts, navigation corresponds to the evolution of a physical system through configuration space; in AI contexts, to the traversal of a reasoning graph; in financial contexts, to movement through market states. The structural problem is the same in all domains: from a current reference configuration, identify a coherent continuation within the unchanged Library. The foundation does not need to specify a domain-specific navigation algorithm. Those interpretations belong to later constructions.

content.text: The important distinction is therefore between ontology and traversal. The Library supplies the unchanged relational totality. Path structure supplies candidate ordered continuations. Observer-relative resolution determines which distinctions remain coherent. Persistence requires those distinctions to remain maintainable. Navigation is the resulting problem of continuing along the surviving relational structure.

content.text: Navigation is the continuation problem that all domains share. In physical contexts, navigation corresponds to the evolution of a physical system through configuration space; in AI contexts, to the traversal of a reasoning graph; in financial contexts, to movement through market states. The foundation therefore establishes the common continuation problem without requiring a domain-specific navigation algorithm.

content.text: The coherent continuation space consists of paths extending the current history whose transitions remain coherent for observer O.
content.interpretation: The observer does not receive a newly generated future. It is relationally situated within the unchanged totality and can sustain only those continuations whose distinctions remain coherent at its resolution.

content.interpretation: Observer-relative navigation narrows the continuation relation without narrowing the underlying Library.

content.text: The coherence relation is explicitly relational. It is not a property possessed by x_i, x_{i+1}, or a path independently of the observer and its reference conditions. The same configurations may therefore participate in different accessible continuation structures for different observers. This is the point at which navigation becomes domain-neutral: physical systems, AI reasoning systems, financial systems, and other structured domains can instantiate different observer-relative resolutions over the same foundational relation without requiring separate ontologies.

content.title: Ontology and Accessibility Remain Distinct
content.text: Observer-relative restriction does not alter Library membership.
content.interpretation: A configuration can fail to belong to the currently sustainable continuation relation while remaining fully contained in the Library.

content.text: Thus the observer does not select from a Library that is being generated around it. Rather, the observer establishes a relational reference within the unchanged totality and evaluates which existing path continuations remain coherent relative to that reference. The resulting continuation set may be restricted even though the underlying Library is not. A configuration excluded by observer-relative coherence is not removed from \mathcal{M}, nor is it assigned to an ontological future that has failed to occur. It simply does not belong to the continuation relation currently sustainable by O under the specified reference conditions.

content.interpretation: Observer-relative inaccessibility is a restriction of traversal, not erasure from the underlying totality.

content.text: Persistence can therefore be expressed as the maintenance of coherent ordered transitions. For a traversal \gamma=(x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_n), persistence for O requires that each relevant transition remain above the observer's effective resolution condition. The resulting sequence is not a sequence of newly generated Library states. It is an ordered traversal relation established over the unchanged totality.

content.text: The traveler changes places; the road does not become.

The traveler denotes the observer as a persistent relational structure. Changing places denotes a change in observer-relative reference x_n and maintained history h_n. The road denotes the static Library 𝓜, whose membership and totality remain unchanged under traversal.

An observer history is an ordered relational structure embedded within the static Library, not a process that generates or modifies the Library. Let O denote an observer and let x_0,x_1,\ldots,x_n ∈ 𝓜 denote configurations related by an observer-maintained sequence, with x_n representing the observer's current relational reference.

content.title: Observer history
content.text: The observer history is the ordered sequence of configurations maintained by the observer.
content.interpretation: The sequence records abstract traversal ordering. The index n does not represent physical time, duration, causality, or any other physical quantity.

content.text: The Library is not correspondingly ordered into successive ontological states. Its totality remains invariant under traversal, expressed formally by ∀i, 𝓜_i = 𝓜. The indexed notation is only a device for stating invariance; it does not imply that multiple temporal copies of the Library exist. The observer changes relational reference from one configuration to another while the total configuration domain remains unchanged.

This establishes the separation between the Library, the observer, and the observer-relative continuation structure. The Library is the static, maximally complete totality 𝓜. The observer is represented structurally by its persistent chain of maintained distinctions and its current relational reference x_n. The coherent continuation relation is evaluated over the unchanged whole 𝓜 rather than over a locally generated future region.

For a given observer O and history h_n with current reference x_n, the full continuation space contains paths already represented within the Library that begin at x_n. The observer-relative coherent continuation set is obtained by applying the canonical coherence relation to those paths.

content.title: Coherent continuation
content.text: The observer-relative coherent continuation set is
content.interpretation: A continuation survives for observer O when its transitions remain distinguishable at or above the observer's resolution floor I_N(O).

content.text: The use of the canonical coherence relation is deliberate. No separate γ_noise threshold is required at this foundational level. The observer-relative resolution floor I_N(O) already enters the chain through δ_O := μ_O(x ⊕ y) and 𝓒(γ | O). Introducing a second threshold without an independent definition would duplicate the same filtering role and obscure the dependency structure.

The explicit dependence on the current reference x_n remains important even though the canonical continuation notation Γ_O(h_n) is sufficient to identify that reference through the final element of h_n. Navigation does not move through a Library that is being generated ahead of the observer. Instead, navigation changes the observer's relational reference within an already complete totality.

The observer's new state therefore changes its history and current reference while leaving 𝓜 unchanged. In this sense, an observer worldline is represented as a relational structure extending across the totality: the ordered sequence records the traversal maintained by the observer, while the configurations related by that sequence remain members of the same static Library.

The observer is consequently relationally situated with respect to the whole Library rather than assigned a privileged local container. A current reference configuration establishes the relation from which coherence is evaluated, but it does not partition the Library into ontologically separate past, present, and future regions. Past and future are therefore traversal orderings within the observer's history rather than intrinsic regions of 𝓜.

A configuration occurring earlier in the history is not thereby assigned permanent membership in a designated past region, and a coherent continuation is not generated into a corresponding future region. Both are configurations represented within the same totality and related differently by the observer's ordered history.

content.title: Library membership versus accessibility
content.text: The existence of a path in the Library does not imply observer-relative coherence.
content.interpretation: Library representation and observer-relative survivorship are distinct relations.

content.text: Conversely, failure of a path to satisfy the observer-relative coherence condition does not remove that path from 𝓜. Survivorship filters the observer's maintained traversal relation; it does not shrink, rewrite, or erase the underlying totality. The observer therefore experiences a restricted continuation space without requiring the ontology itself to be restricted.

content.title: Coherent subset relation
content.text: The coherent continuation set is a subset of the full continuation space.
content.interpretation: The restriction is observer-relative and epistemic/accessibility-based within the formal model, not an ontological deletion from the Library.

content.title: Admissible continuation requirement
content.text: The model requires every admissible observer-relative reference configuration to admit at least one coherent continuation.
content.interpretation: This is an explicit continuation requirement of the model. It is not claimed to be a theorem derived from maximality alone.

content.text: The distinction between maximality and continuation must be preserved. Maximal static totality establishes that Library membership does not depend upon a privileged construction history or external generating event. The non-emptiness condition separately requires that an admissible observer-relative reference support continued coherent traversal. These are logically distinct statements.

The continuation structure may contain many candidate paths even when only a restricted subset remains coherent for a particular observer. The difference Ω(x_n) \ Γ_O(h_n) therefore represents paths that remain represented within the Library but do not survive the observer's present coherence condition.

content.title: Navigation

content.interpretation: The operator specifies the continuation space available to navigation but does not prescribe how a particular continuation is selected.

content.text: The navigation operator does not specify an algorithm, optimization rule, probability distribution, conscious choice, agency, or physical mechanism. It states only that navigation is the traversal or selection of a continuation within the observer-relative coherent continuation set. When navigation produces a new observer state, the relational variables change; the Library does not.

The road does not become as the traveler moves; rather, the traveler changes relational reference within a road that is already complete. Apparent temporal progression and restriction of available continuation are therefore properties of the observer's changing relation to 𝓜, not successive ontological states of 𝓜 itself.

content.text: The axiomatic floor has now established a formal configuration domain, its XOR closure as the Library, observerhood as a persistent structural property, observer-relative resolution through I_N(O), and coherence as a relation between paths and observers. Only at this point is it appropriate to introduce geometric language. Noor Swirl Field Geometry (NSFG) does not begin by assuming a geometry in which configurations exist. Rather, geometry appears as a description of the relational structure formed by configurations, accessible transitions, and families of paths that remain coherent for a given observer.
Before the field has a shape, the paths must have relations.

The phrase 'field has a shape' is metaphorical. At this stage no physical space or geometric container has been introduced. The established formal relations between configurations and coherent paths are sufficient to motivate a geometric description of their connectivity.
For an observer O, the coherent paths through the Library form a restricted family of traversable structures. Define the observer-coherent path family by

content.title: Observer-coherent path family

content.interpretation: The set \(\Gamma_O\) contains paths that remain coherent relative to O. It is therefore not a universal set of physically preferred trajectories. A path belongs to \(\Gamma_O\) because of its relation to the observer's resolution structure, not because coherence is an intrinsic property of the path alone.

content.text: A path does not glow alone; it remains visible in relation.
The 'glow' is a metaphor for membership in the observer-relative coherent path family. The formal content is the condition \(\mathcal{C}(\gamma \mid O)=1\).
The same construction permits a local description around an accessible configuration x. Let

content.title: Observer-relative accessibility neighborhood
content.text: U_O(x) = \{y \in \mathcal{M} \mid y\text{ is reachable from }x\text{ by an }O\text{-coherent path segment}\}
content.latex: U_O(x) = \{y \in \mathcal{M} \mid y\text{ is reachable from }x\text{ by an }O\text{-coherent path segment}\}

It is an accessibility neighborhood: the collection of configurations that can be reached from x through path segments that remain coherent relative to O. If later NSFG work supplies additional structure, this relational neighborhood may acquire familiar geometric interpretations. The axiomatic floor itself does not require such an interpretation.

content.text: Nearness begins as continuation, not distance.

The word 'nearness' refers initially to relational reachability rather than spatial separation. Two configurations may be locally related because a coherent path connects them, without the primer assigning them coordinates, distances, or a physical location.
The accessible relational structure can therefore be represented as a graph. Define

content.title: Accessible relational graph
content.text: G_O := (A_O,E_O)
content.interpretation: Here A_O is the observer-accessible state set already established by the preceding construction, while E_O records coherent relational connections between accessible configurations.

content.title: Graph edge relation
content.text: (x,y) \in E_O \iff x\to y\text{ is an }O\text{-coherent transition}

Depending on the requirements of a later formalism, the relation may be represented as directed, preserving transition orientation, or as undirected when orientation is not relevant. Neither choice is imposed by the axiomatic floor.

content.text: The points are not yet a world; their surviving relations are its first shape.

The 'points' are configurations in A_O, while the 'surviving relations' are elements of E_O. 'World' is descriptive language for the resulting accessible relational structure, not a claim that a physical spacetime has already been constructed.

The word 'field' in Noor Swirl Field Geometry should therefore be understood initially as descriptive rather than ontological. A field, at this level, is a structured distribution of relational possibilities: which configurations are connected, which transitions remain coherent, and how families of coherent paths organize around persistent configurations. No additional field substance is introduced.
The field is not another thing; it is the pattern of relations.
The 'field' denotes an organized relational structure derived from configurations, accessibility, and coherent transitions. It is not a new primitive entity and is not treated as a physical medium.

Likewise, 'geometry' is descriptive language for the structure of relations among accessible configurations and paths. At this stage, geometry means that the relational system has organization that can be studied in terms of neighborhoods, connectivity, path families, adjacency, and continuation. This is deliberately weaker than assuming a metric space or differentiable manifold.

No metric tensor, coordinate chart, manifold structure, curvature tensor, or other conventional geometric object is required by the axiomatic floor. Such structures may become useful later if they can be derived or consistently introduced as downstream constructions.
Geometry begins where relations acquire shape.
The 'shape' is the organization of relational connectivity. It does not yet mean Euclidean, Riemannian, Lorentzian, or any other physical geometry.

The term 'swirl' provides an intuition for how locally structured path families may organize around persistent relational configurations. A persistent configuration can participate in many coherent continuations, while the observer-relative resolution threshold restricts which transitions remain admissible. The resulting family of paths can possess local structure: paths may converge, diverge, braid, circulate, or repeatedly organize around persistent configurations. 'Swirl' names this qualitative possibility of structured local path organization.

The term is intentionally intuitive at this stage. It does not assert literal rotational motion, angular momentum, fluid dynamics, or a physical vortex. In particular, no temporal evolution or physical movement is implied merely by the word 'flow'. The underlying construction remains a set of configurations and relations among paths.
Where many surviving paths gather, a shape may turn without anything yet moving.

The apparent 'turning' describes the organization of path connectivity, not physical rotation. The statement deliberately avoids introducing time, motion, or a dynamical medium before those concepts have been independently established.

The graph representation makes the geometric interpretation concrete without requiring physical geometry. The accessible configurations form vertices, while coherent transitions form edges. Families of coherent paths then become sequences through this relational graph. Local structure can be studied through the accessible neighborhood U_O(x), while larger-scale structure can be studied through connected path families and continuation spaces.

content.text: This representation preserves the foundational ordering established by the primer: the graph is constructed from accessibility and coherence; coherence is constructed from observer-relative distinguishability; distinguishability depends on I_N(O) and the observer-relative magnitude evaluation μ_O; observerhood is derived from persistent distinctions; and the Library itself is defined as XOR closure. Geometry therefore enters downstream of the axiomatic floor rather than being smuggled into it at the beginning.
First distinction, then survival, then relation, then shape.

Each word corresponds to a stage of the dependency chain. Distinction comes from XOR; survival is expressed through persistent resolvable transitions; relation produces coherent accessibility; and the resulting connectivity admits geometric description.

This distinction is important because NSFG, at this stage, is not claiming that the accessible graph G_O is physical spacetime. The graph is a formal relational object. A later theory may investigate whether familiar physical geometries can emerge from additional structure imposed upon, or derived from, these relational configurations. Such a derivation would be a subsequent result, not a premise of this primer.

The 'map' is the formal relational representation G_O. 'The world' refers only to a possible later physical interpretation. The metaphor therefore marks the boundary between formal relational geometry and subsequent physical theory.

In physical contexts, the relational graph G_O may be interpreted as a configuration space or phase space; in AI contexts, as a reasoning graph or knowledge structure; in financial contexts, as a market-state graph or opportunity space. The underlying formal structure is unchanged across these interpretations. The field is the organization of relations; the geometry is the structure of that organization; the domain-specific meaning belongs to the observer's resolution and interpretation of the relations.

The cross-domain character of this interpretation does not introduce separate foundational ontologies for physics, AI, finance, or other domains. The formal chain remains domain-neutral. Domain-specific meaning enters through the observer-relative magnitude evaluation μ_O, resolution floor I_N(O), resulting coherence relation, and the downstream interpretation assigned to the accessible relational structure.
The map is the same; the territory it describes changes with the traveler.

section.title: The Axiomatic Dependency Chain
section.purpose: Compress the entire primer into one explicit derivational architecture, distinguish axioms, definitions, invariants, derived requirements, and downstream consequences, and establish the boundary between the static Library and observer-relative traversal.
section.poetic_cipher: The whole is everywhere; coherence follows wherever the reference falls.
section.cipher_explanation: The final cipher compresses the dependency architecture. The whole represents the static, maximally complete Library and its lack of a privileged worldline or describable exterior. content.text: The primer can now be compressed into a single dependency architecture. The essential point is not merely the order in which concepts appear, but the logical status of each concept and the strict separation between the Library itself and the observer's relation to it. XOR is the sole primitive operation of distinction. D is the minimal formal domain required for XOR to operate. G specifies the generating configurations used to characterize the XOR closure. The Library \(\mathcal{M}\) is the static, maximally complete totality characterized by closure under XOR together with self-containment and the absence of a privileged definable exterior. Closure is a formal property, not a temporal generation process. Traversal does not enlarge, modify, or generate the Library. Instead, an observer is relationally situated with respect to the whole \(\mathcal{M}\), establishes an admissible reference configuration, and evaluates distinctions, persistence, coherence, accessibility, and continuation relative to that reference, its history, and its observer-specific resolution. Apparent temporal ordering, locality, increasing complexity, and restricted possibility therefore belong to the observer's traversal relation rather than to an intrinsic evolution of the Library. No later concept is permitted to become a hidden premise of an earlier one.

XOR is the only primitive. The Library is the static totality characterized by XOR closure. No worldline owns the whole. The observer is relationally situated within the whole. The reference determines the experienced coherent structure. Coherence is the relation between observer, history, reference, and path. Reality is what remains accessible without shrinking the totality. Law is the regularity of surviving traversals. Navigation is continuation through the unchanged whole.

A philosophical distinction must be maintained throughout the interpretation of this framework. Ontologically, the Library is static and complete. No new configurations are generated, and no Library member is ever added or removed. Epistemically, however, an observer may discover new coherence relations, experience novel paths, and construct new accessible subsets as its relational history, resolution, or reference changes. The distinction is essential: the Library does not grow, but the observer's relation to it may become richer. This permits genuine discovery and learning without requiring the Library to evolve or generate new ontology. Discovery is possible because what is discovered is already represented within the totality; what changes is the observer's relation to it.
The mountain does not grow; the climber's view expands.

The mountain is the static Library. The climber's view is the observer's accessible relation to that Library. The mountain does not change; the climber's perspective, resolution, history, and accessible paths may become richer.

content.title: Step 1 — Primitive distinction
content.text: AXIOM. The axiomatic floor begins with one primitive operation: XOR. No physical object, space, time, observer, causality, matter, energy, or information substance is assumed. XOR expresses distinction: equal inputs cancel to 0, while unequal inputs produce 1.

content.title: Step 2 — Formal configuration domain
content.text: DEFINITION. D is the minimal formal domain containing the configurations required for \(\oplus\) to have operands. D is introduced because an operation requires a domain on which it acts. D is not physical space, spacetime, matter, energy, information, or an additional physical ontology.

content.title: Step 3 — Static maximally complete Library
content.text: DEFINITION + INVARIANT. The Library is the maximally complete static totality characterized by XOR closure over D, containing the specified generating configurations G, and satisfying self-containment with respect to its formal resources. Closure specifies a formal property of the totality; it is not a temporal generation mechanism. The Library does not progressively come into existence through repeated XOR operations. There is one unchanged totality rather than a succession of increasingly complete Libraries. Membership in the Library does not imply persistence, coherence, physicality, observability, accessibility, consciousness, or causal participation.

content.title: Step 4 — No privileged worldline or universal reference
content.text: INVARIANT. No configuration, worldline, traversal history, or observer is privileged as the universal origin from which the whole Library must be constructed or evaluated. Maximality is structurally connected to reference-frame neutrality, not merely to maximizing the number of configurations.
content.latex: \nexists\,w_{\mathrm{priv}}\;\text{such that}\;w_{\mathrm{priv}}\;\text{is the unique universal reference for}\;\mathcal{M}

content.title: Step 5 — No describable privileged exterior
content.text: CONSEQUENCE. An external candidate may be proposed informally, but if it is describable using the same formal machinery, it belongs to the formal domain to which the closure applies. The closure therefore establishes a formal boundary condition on describable exteriors. It does not independently assert that every informal notion of literal physical exteriority is impossible.
content.latex: \Omega\;\text{describable within the same formal machinery}\Rightarrow\Omega\in D, \qquad \Omega\;\text{XOR-generable}\Rightarrow\Omega\in\mathcal{M}

content.title: Step 6 — Whole-Library relationality
content.text: INVARIANT. The observer is relationally situated with respect to the whole Library rather than occupying an ontologically isolated local region from which the remainder of the Library is external. Locality is therefore a property of relational access and traversal, not a partition of the Library into an observer-containing region and an intrinsically external remainder.
content.latex: O \subseteq \mathcal{M}, \qquad O\;\text{is relationally evaluated with respect to}\;\mathcal{M}

content.title: Step 7 — Admissible reference configuration
content.text: DEFINITION. An admissible reference configuration is a configuration capable of instantiating an observer-relative reference state under the model's admissibility conditions. The reference configuration does not create a new ontological layer or select a new Library. It specifies the configuration from which the observer's current relational evaluation is made.

content.title: Step 8 — Observer
content.text: DEFINITION. Observerhood is introduced structurally rather than psychologically. An observer is a configuration capable of maintaining a persistent chain of resolvable distinctions. The definition does not require consciousness, intention, agency, perception, or a human subject.

content.title: Step 9 — Observer-relative resolution
content.text: DEFINITION. Each observer O is assigned an effective minimum distinction magnitude that it can maintain as a stable distinction. \(I_N(O)\) belongs to the observer relation rather than to the Library as a universal constant. No universal numerical value for \(I_N\) is supplied by the axiomatic floor, and \(I_N\) is not identified with the ordinary Planck scale.

content.title: Step 10 — Observer-relative distinguishability from XOR
content.text: DEFINITION DERIVED FROM THE PRIMITIVE. The distinction between x and y is first produced by the primitive operation \(x\oplus y\). The observer does not introduce a second primitive operation to measure that distinction; rather, observer-relative resolution supplies the effective magnitude with which the resulting distinction is evaluated. This closes the dependency gap between XOR and distinguishability without assigning a universal metric to the Library. Two configurations may therefore be distinguishable for one observer and indistinguishable for another without requiring either configuration to cease existing in the Library. Indistinguishability is a relational statement, not ontological deletion.
content.interpretation: The primitive XOR produces the distinction; \(\mu_O\) supplies its observer-relative effective magnitude. The foundational system therefore does not require a universal metric to be imposed on the Library.

content.title: Step 10 — Observer-relative distinguishability thresholds
content.text: Observer-relative distinguishability is determined by comparison between the effective magnitude of a distinction and the observer's resolution floor.
content.latex: x \approx_O y \iff \delta_O(x,y) < I_N(O), \qquad x \not\approx_O y \iff \delta_O(x,y) \geq I_N(O)

content.text: μ_O is deliberately underspecified at the foundational level. Its specific functional form is a downstream construction that may vary by domain. In a physical domain, μ_O may represent a resolution scale related to measurement precision; in an AI domain, it may represent a symbolic distinctness threshold; in a financial domain, it may represent a minimum actionable distinction. The structural relation \(\delta_O(x,y):=\mu_O(x\oplus y)\) remains unchanged; only the interpretation of μ_O varies. The foundational primitive remains Boolean XOR, so the primitive itself supplies a distinction floor rather than a universal continuous geometry. Any continuous magnitude associated with a distinction is therefore an observer- and domain-relative downstream evaluation, not an additional primitive.
The measure is not fixed; it is given by the hand that holds it.

μ_O is not assigned a universal functional form. Its specific interpretation depends on the observer's structural capacity and domain context. The hand that holds the measure determines its effective scale while the underlying XOR distinction remains unchanged.

content.title: Step 11 — Observer history and abstract traversal ordering
content.text: DEFINITION. Observer history is an ordered sequence relevant to the observer's current relational evaluation. The sequence index is an abstract traversal index rather than a primitive physical time coordinate. It does not partition the Library into intrinsic past, present, and future regions.

content.title: Step 12 — Observer-relative coherence
content.text: DEFINITION. Coherence evaluates whether a traversal remains coherent relative to observer O, relevant history h, and current reference configuration x. Coherence is relational rather than intrinsic to a path considered in isolation. The mathematical structure remains domain-neutral and may later be interpreted in physical, AI, financial, or other domain-specific contexts.

content.title: Step 12 — Path coherence
content.text: A path is coherent when each transition in the relevant traversal satisfies the observer-relative coherence condition.

content.title: Step 13 — Observer-accessible reality
content.text: DEFINITION. Observer-accessible reality is the subset of the Library reachable through observer-maintained coherent traversal from the relevant relational state. A configuration outside this accessible subset is not removed from the Library. Accessibility therefore does not create ontology, and inaccessibility does not constitute erasure.

content.title: Step 14 — Whole-Library continuation space
content.text: DEFINITION. Continuation is evaluated over the static Library. The Library does not generate a future when the observer reaches x. Rather, the observer's traversal relation identifies ordered continuations already represented within the unchanged totality.

content.title: Step 15 — Nonempty coherent continuation
content.text: DERIVED REQUIREMENT. For every admissible observer-relative reference configuration, the model requires at least one observer-coherent continuation. This requirement is not a theorem obtained from XOR closure alone. It is a structural condition imposed on the observer-relative traversal model.

content.title: Step 16 — Observer-relative coherent continuation
content.text: DEFINITION. The coherent continuation space is a restricted relational structure over the unchanged Library. The restriction belongs to observer-relative evaluation, not to Library membership. No future configuration is generated when a continuation is selected; the observer traverses a path already represented within the static totality.

content.title: Step 17 — Emergent temporal and complexity structure
content.text: CONSEQUENCE. Ordered traversal through an unchanged Library can produce an observer-relative experience of temporal direction, locality, increasing complexity, and past/future distinction. The Library does not evolve from simple to complex. What changes is the observer's relational state and history.
content.latex: \mathcal{M}_i=\mathcal{M}\;\forall i, \qquad O(h_i)\ne O(h_j)\;\text{may hold for}\;i\ne j

content.title: Step 18 — Emergent regularity
content.text: CONSEQUENCE. Repeated survivorship can produce regularities that are describable in law-like terms. Such regularity is descriptive and derived. It is not an additional element of the axiom set and does not constitute a derivation of any particular physical law.
content.latex: L_O(x,y)=1\iff x\to y\;\text{is a stable recurring transition across an appropriate family of O-accessible traversals}

content.title: Step 18 — Probabilistic form of emergent regularity
content.text: Where an observer-accessible ensemble is defined, recurring transitions may be represented probabilistically.

content.title: Step 19 — Navigation
content.text: DEFINITION / DOWNSTREAM THRESHOLD. Navigation is the traversal or selection of a continuation within the observer-relative coherent continuation space. It does not require the Library to generate a future. It is a continuation problem over an unchanged totality and therefore marks the boundary of the axiomatic primer and the entry point for subsequent NSFG work.

content.title: Step 20 — Cross-Domain Applicability
content.text: STRUCTURAL CONSEQUENCE. The foundation defined by this primer is domain-neutral. The same structural relations—distinguishability, coherence, accessibility, survivorship, continuation, and navigation—apply to physics, AI, finance, and any other domain that can be represented as observer-relative traversal through a static Library. Domains differ in the interpretation of observer-relative resolution \(I_N(O)\), the distinguishability evaluation \(\delta_O\), and the resulting coherence relation, not in the foundational ontology. No domain-specific axioms are required merely to apply the formal architecture to a new area. Domain-specific assumptions may be introduced downstream, but they must remain downstream and must not be retroactively inserted into the axiomatic floor.

For example, in a physical domain, \(I_N(O)\) may be interpreted as a resolution scale related to measurement precision, and μ_O may map XOR distinctions to effective physical distinguishability. In an AI domain, \(I_N(O)\) may represent the effective resolution of a symbolic reasoning system, and μ_O may map symbolic differences to a distinctness measure. In a financial domain, \(I_N(O)\) may represent a minimum actionable price movement or information threshold, and μ_O may map market-state distinctions to actionable distinguishability. The structural relations remain unchanged; only the interpretation of \(I_N(O)\) and μ_O varies.
One seed grows into oak, vine, and wheat; the soil is the same.

The seed is the foundational architecture. The oak, vine, and wheat are physics, AI, and finance. The soil is the Library and its relational structure. The same foundation supports multiple domains without requiring domain-specific assumptions to be inserted into the axiomatic floor.

The dependency architecture can therefore be compressed as follows: XOR supplies distinction; D supplies the formal operand domain; G supplies generating configurations; XOR closure characterizes the static Library; self-containment and maximality eliminate a privileged describable exterior; reference neutrality eliminates a privileged worldline; whole-Library relationality establishes the observer's position within the totality; admissible reference establishes the current relational state; observerhood supplies a structurally persistent evaluator; \(I_N(O)\) supplies observer-relative resolution; XOR-induced distinction evaluated through μ_O supplies \(\delta_O\); history supplies traversal ordering; coherence evaluates survivorship; accessibility identifies the observer-relative accessible subset; \(\Omega(x)\) represents continuation through the unchanged Library; \(\Gamma_O(h,x)\) restricts that continuation by observer-relative coherence; navigation selects or traverses within that space; emergent regularity describes recurring survivorship; and cross-domain applicability permits downstream interpretations without altering the foundational ontology.

The compact dependency chain is: \(\oplus\to D\to G\to\operatorname{Closure}_D(\oplus,G)=\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{static,max}}\to\text{no privileged exterior}\to\text{no privileged worldline/reference}\to\text{whole-Library relationality}\to x\in\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{admissible}}\to O\to I_N(O)\to(x\oplus y)\to\mu_O\to\delta_O\to h\to\mathcal{C}(\gamma\mid O,h,x)\to A_O(h,x)\to\Omega(x)\to\Gamma_O(h,x)\ne\varnothing\to\text{observer-relative traversal}\to\text{emergent temporal/complexity structure}\to L_O\to N_O(h,x)\to\Gamma_O(h,x)\to\text{cross-domain applicability}\).

content.text: Three layers must remain formally separated. First is the Library \(\mathcal{M}\), the static, eternally maximally complete totality characterized by XOR closure and self-containment. Second is the observer state \(O(h_i)\), consisting of the observer configuration and history relevant to the current relational evaluation. Third is the observer-relative structure \(\Gamma_O(h_i,x_i)\), \(\mathcal{C}(\gamma\mid O,h_i,x_i)\), and \(A_O(h_i,x_i)\), consisting of relational structures evaluated over the unchanged Library. These layers must not be collapsed. The Library does not become the observer's history, the observer's history does not become the Library, and the coherent continuation space does not become the totality itself.

The axiomatic floor ends before physical or domain-specific interpretation. It establishes a formal architecture from distinction to formal closure, from closure to static maximal totality, from maximality and self-containment to the absence of privileged exteriors and worldlines, from whole-Library relationality to arbitrary admissible reference, from XOR-induced distinction to observer-relative resolution and coherence, from coherence to accessibility and continuation, and from restricted continuation to navigation. The next step is therefore not to add another foundational primitive or to generate a new Library state, but to investigate what mathematical structure can be built on the coherent continuation space already defined.

The primer ends at navigation and explicitly establishes cross-domain applicability. Subsequent NSFG research may investigate the geometry, dynamics, topology, symbolic representation, or physical interpretation of coherent navigation, while domain-specific downstream work may apply the same foundation to AI, finance, or other domains. All such work must preserve the distinction between the static Library \(\mathcal{M}\) and observer-relative traversal over \(\mathcal{M}\). Downstream models may introduce additional assumptions, but those assumptions must remain downstream and must not be retroactively inserted into the axiomatic floor.

appendix_A.title: Mathematical Reference Sheet
appendix_A.subtitle: Canonical Definitions, Notation, and Dependency Vocabulary
appendix_A.purpose: Provide the complete mathematical vocabulary required to reconstruct the formal content of the primer without consulting external material. This appendix is normative for notation and formal definitions. It does not introduce new axioms, physical assumptions, or downstream NSFG mechanisms.
appendix_A.scope: The reference sheet specifies the formal domain, primitive XOR operation, generating configurations, XOR closure, observer structure, observer-relative resolution, observer-relative magnitude evaluation, distinguishability, persistence, coherence, accessible reality, continuation spaces, survivorship, navigation, and the resulting observer-relative graph structure.
appendix_A.notation_rule: Symbols defined in this appendix are canonical for the primer. Interpretive prose may use descriptive language, but mathematical statements should use these definitions unless a later document explicitly extends or refines them.

axiomatic_status.axiom: A_⊕ : ⊕ is the primitive operation of distinction.
axiomatic_status.important_constraint: All other entries in this appendix are definitions, constructions, or consequences of the axiom together with ordinary mathematical inference.

formal_domain.definition: A minimal formal domain containing the configurations required for the primitive operation ⊕ to have operands.
formal_domain.constraint: D is not physical space, spacetime, matter, energy, information, or any other physical ontology.

generators.definition: A specified subset of D containing the configurations from which the XOR closure is generated.
generators.interpretation: G identifies the required generating configurations for the formal closure. It is not an additional primitive operation or physical axiom.

xor.interpretation: XOR is treated at the axiomatic floor as distinction. Equal configurations cancel; unequal configurations produce distinction.

closure.definition: The smallest subset 𝓜 of D containing G and closed under ⊕.
closure.minimality_condition: If S ⊆ D is closed under ⊕ and G ⊆ S, then 𝓜 ⊆ S.
closure.important_constraint: The Library is a set closed under an operation. XOR itself is not a closed set.
closure.interpretation: The Library is generated by closure rather than introduced as an independent ontological primitive.

library.definition: The maximally complete unbounded totality satisfying closure under XOR and self-containment with no definable privileged exterior. 𝓜 is a dimensionally undifferentiated complete relational totality, not a grid, container, temporal sequence, or singularity.

formal_characterization.self_containment: ¬∃ z ∉ 𝓜 such that z is definable within the system using only ⊕ and elements of 𝓜 over D as a privileged exterior
formal_characterization.equivalence: 𝓜 is closed under XOR, self-contained with respect to its formal resources, and contains no privileged definable exterior

library.equation: 𝓜 is defined by property, not by construction: 𝓜 is the maximally complete unbounded totality satisfying XOR closure together with self-containment and absence of a privileged definable exterior. Closure_D describes a property of 𝓜, not a temporal or generative process.
library.self_containment_condition: No element outside 𝓜 is definable within the system as a privileged exterior using the formal resources of the system.
library.whole_library_invariant: At every abstract traversal step, the observer is relationally situated with respect to the entire static Library 𝓜. The observer does not encounter a temporal slice, local neighborhood, generated future, or pre-filtered coherent subset.
library.static_totality_condition: 𝓜 does not change as observer history changes. Changes in observer state, accessibility, distinguishability, or coherent continuation alter the observer's relation to 𝓜, not 𝓜 itself.
library.coherence_membership_separation: Membership in 𝓜 is prior to and independent of observer-relative coherence. Coherence determines whether a traversal relation can be maintained by an observer; it does not determine Library membership.
library.unboundedness_condition: 𝓜 has no privileged boundary, terminal region, or excluded coordinate whose status would determine where coherent traversal is permitted. If an arbitrary x ∈ 𝓜 could function as a coherence boundary merely because of its location in 𝓜, then the totality would possess an observer-independent bound or privileged reference condition inconsistent with its unbounded self-contained definition.
library.no_privileged_origin_condition: No x ∈ 𝓜 is privileged as an ontological origin, reference frame, or starting state. Any x ∈ 𝓜 may serve as the relational origin from which observer-relative coherence is evaluated without becoming the origin or generator of 𝓜.
library.arbitrary_origin_coherence_invariant: For an observer O situated at any arbitrary x ∈ 𝓜, the coherent continuation relation must remain nonempty above the observer's operative coherence threshold. The guarantee is not supplied by x being special, but by the combination of maximal completeness, unboundedness, whole-Library relation, and absence of a privileged exterior reference frame.
library.arbitrary_origin_coherence_formalization: ∀x ∈ 𝓜, ∀O with a defined resolution floor I_N(O), ∃γ ∈ Path(𝓜) such that γ begins at x and 𝓒(γ | O) = 1, provided the observer's state admits continuation. No x is excluded from coherent traversal merely by its coordinate within 𝓜.
library.why_arbitrary_origin_is_required: If some x ∈ 𝓜 admitted no coherent continuation solely because of its location, then x would function as a boundary of the unbounded totality or coherence would depend upon a privileged reference frame. Either result would introduce structure external to the relational totality. The absence of a privileged perspective therefore requires coherence to be relocatable: the same relational mechanism must apply from any arbitrary point.
library.whole_library_relation: The observer does not first receive a local subset of 𝓜 and then navigate that subset. At every abstract step the observer is relationally situated with respect to the whole 𝓜. The minimal coherent continuation set emerges only from the relation between that whole totality and the observer's current state, history, and resolution capacity.
library.coherent_continuation_note: For any x ∈ 𝓜, XOR closure ensures that relational operations remain within the Library rather than terminating at an external configuration. The stronger requirement of a nonempty coherent continuation follows from whole-Library traversal together with unboundedness and absence of a privileged reference frame. I_N(O) filters distinguishability and coherence; it does not create, delete, or bound 𝓜.
library.continuation_not_generation: A coherent continuation is not a configuration generated into existence after x. It is an observer-relative traversal relation among configurations already contained in the static totality 𝓜.

termination_singleton.definition: Unique singleton where XOR completes and recursive bounce degenerates
properties: (x ⊕ y) ⊕ y = x degenerates when y = 0
Single equivalence class under x ∼ y ⇔ x ⊕ y = 0
Where distinction completes, no new relation is generated
termination_singleton.relation_to_library: 𝒵 ⊂ 𝓜, interior termination, not exterior. Complementary as termination versus non-degenerate distinction: 𝓜\𝒵 represents configurations participating in non-degenerate relational distinction, while 𝒵 represents completed distinction.

library.generating_set_note: G is not a primitive that builds 𝓜. Any G ⊆ 𝓜 may serve as an addressable generating description of portions of the closure, but G is not an ontological origin of 𝓜. Generation language here describes algebraic addressability, not temporal construction.
library.non_erasure_rule: x ∉ A_O does not imply x ∉ 𝓜. Failure of observer-relative accessibility, coherence, or distinguishability does not erase a configuration from the totality. Reaching 𝒵 is collapse of distinguishability, not erasure.
library.observer_relocation_invariant: Relocating the observer's relational origin from x to any arbitrary y ∈ 𝓜 does not change the underlying Library or invoke a new external reference frame. Only the observer-relative coherence relation changes.
library.reference_frame_independence: There is no privileged coordinate, state, history, or world line from which coherence is intrinsically defined. Coherence is determined relative to the current observer configuration and history, wherever that observer is situated within 𝓜.
library.noise_without_internal_relation: Viewed from a hypothetical perspective external to 𝓜, the totality need not exhibit the observer-relative structure that appears internally. Such a perspective supplies no useful privileged ordering because the Library's structure is relationally self-contained. The observer-relative coherent world line is therefore not imposed by an external ordering; it emerges from the relation of an observer to the totality itself.

no_privileged_exterior.formal_condition: Ω ∉ 𝓜 may be proposed as an external candidate.
no_privileged_exterior.closure_consequence: If Ω is internally describable using the same formal machinery, then Ω ∈ D; if Ω is XOR-generable from D, then Ω ∈ 𝓜 by closure property: 𝓜 is the unique totality with ∀x,y ∈ 𝓜, x ⊕ y ∈ 𝓜 and no definable exterior. May be described as Closure_D only as property, not process.
no_privileged_exterior.termination_singleton_is_not_exterior: 𝒵 := {z | z ⊕ z = z} = {0} ⊂ 𝓜 satisfies ∀x, x ⊕ x ∈ 𝒵 and 0 ⊕ x = x. 𝒵 is where distinction completes and recursive bounce (x ⊕ y) ⊕ y = x degenerates. 𝒵 is a single equivalence class under x ∼ y ⇔ x ⊕ y = 0 and is complementary as termination versus generation, not as exterior.
no_privileged_exterior.conclusion: A describable privileged exterior cannot remain external to 𝓜. Any candidate definable using ⊕ and elements of 𝓜 over D is already in 𝓜, including 𝒵.
no_privileged_exterior.scope_constraint: This is a formal boundary condition on describable exteriors concerning absence of privileged internal coherence relation supplied by external God's-eye reference; it does not assert that literal physical exteriority is independently impossible, only that no such reference is definable within the system.

observer.definition: A configuration in 𝓜 capable of maintaining a persistent chain of distinctions above its observer-specific resolution floor.
observer.structural_definition: O is an observer iff O can maintain a persistent chain of distinctions that remain resolvable relative to O.
observer.important_constraint: Observerhood is structural and does not imply consciousness, perception, intention, or agency.

resolution.definition: The minimum effective distinction magnitude observer O can maintain as a stable distinction.
resolution.important_constraint: No universal value of I_N is supplied by the axiomatic floor.

magnitude_evaluation.definition: The observer-relative magnitude evaluation function that maps a primitive XOR distinction to an effective magnitude resolvable by observer O. μ_O is monotonic with respect to XOR-derived distinction: if x ⊕ y = 1 and u ⊕ v = 0, then μ_O(x ⊕ y) ≥ μ_O(u ⊕ v). The specific functional form of μ_O is not specified at the foundational level and may vary by domain or observer structure.
magnitude_evaluation.constraint: μ_O is observer-relative and domain-neutral at the foundational level. Its specific form is a downstream construction or domain-specific interpretation.

distinguishability.definition: The observer-relative effective magnitude of the distinction between configurations x and y, obtained by applying the observer-relative magnitude evaluation μ_O to the primitive XOR distinction x ⊕ y.
distinguishability.non_identity_rule: x ≈_O y does not imply x = y.
distinguishability.non_erasure_rule: x ≈_O y does not imply x ∉ 𝓜.
distinguishability.observer_dependence: The same pair of configurations may be distinguishable relative to one observer and indistinguishable relative to another.
distinguishability.derivation_note: δ_O is not an additional primitive. It is derived from the sole primitive distinction operation ⊕ through the observer-relative magnitude evaluation μ_O.
distinguishability.domain_neutrality_note: The formal structure of δ_O is domain-neutral. Domain-specific interpretation enters through the observer-relative evaluation μ_O and resolution floor I_N(O), not through a new foundational distinction operation.

persistence.time_warning: The index i represents abstract ordering and is not yet physical time.
persistence.interpretation: Persistence is the maintenance of observer-resolvable distinctions across an ordered chain.

coherence.coherence_derivation_note: Coherence is derived from δ_O and I_N(O), with δ_O itself derived from μ_O and the primitive XOR distinction. No universal coherence constant is introduced.
coherence.domain_neutrality_note: The coherence condition is domain-neutral. In physical contexts, it may be interpreted as the condition for a worldline to satisfy the equations of motion; in AI contexts, as the condition for a reasoning path to be symbolically consistent; in financial contexts, as the condition for a trading strategy to be coherent across market states. The mathematical structure is the same in all domains.
coherence.binary_condition: 𝓒(γ | O) = 1 iff every transition in γ remains resolvable by O.
coherence.interpretation: Coherence is the relation between a path and an observer.
coherence.noise_threshold_note: No separate γ_noise threshold is introduced. The foundational coherence condition is governed by I_N(O) through δ_O.
coherence.important_constraint: Prefer 𝓒(γ | O) over 𝓒(γ) whenever observer dependence matters.

accessible_reality.accessible_states: A_O = {x ∈ 𝓜 | ∃γ containing x such that 𝓒(γ | O) = 1}
accessible_reality.interpretation: A_O is the subset of the Library accessible through observer-relative coherent traversal.
accessible_reality.non_erasure: x ∉ A_O does not imply x ∉ 𝓜.
accessible_reality.observer_creation_rule: A_O is not ontologically created by O; it is an observer-relative accessibility subset of 𝓜.
accessible_reality.domain_neutrality_note: The construction of A_O is domain-neutral. The domain-specific character of accessibility is determined by the observer-relative resolution I_N(O), magnitude evaluation μ_O, and resulting coherence relation.

continuation.continuation_space: Ω(x) = {γ | γ begins at x and γ is a path contained in 𝓜}
continuation.coherence_condition_note: Coherence is defined in terms of I_N(O) through δ_O. No separate γ_noise threshold is introduced at the foundational level.
continuation.interpretation: Survivorship restricts observer-accessible continuation without deleting non-surviving paths from the represented continuation space.
continuation.future_generation_rule: The Library does not generate future events. Continuation describes represented paths and their observer-relative survivorship.
continuation.domain_neutrality_note: The continuation construction is domain-neutral. Physical, AI, financial, or other domain interpretations differ in the observer-relative structure used to evaluate coherence, not in the underlying continuation space Ω(x).

survivorship.definition: Observer-relative filtering of continuation paths according to the coherence condition 𝓒(γ | O) = 1.
survivorship.interpretation: A path survives relative to O when its transitions remain above O's resolution threshold.
survivorship.deletion_rule: Survivorship does not delete the alternatives contained in Ω(x).
survivorship.domain_neutrality_note: Survivorship is a domain-neutral filtering construction. Its domain-specific interpretation arises from μ_O, I_N(O), and the resulting observer-relative coherence relation.

emergent_regularity.definition: A derived relation representing a stable recurring transition across an appropriate family of O-accessible paths.
emergent_regularity.formal_condition: L_O(x,y) = 1 iff x → y is a stable recurring transition across an appropriate family of O-accessible paths.
emergent_regularity.probabilistic_form: P_O(y | x) ≈ constant over a defined observer-accessible ensemble.
emergent_regularity.domain_neutrality_note: L_O is domain-neutral as a structural relation. Its interpretation as a physical law, reasoning regularity, financial regularity, or other domain-specific regularity is downstream of the observer-relative accessibility structure.
emergent_regularity.important_constraint: L_O is not an element of the axiomatic set A_N.
emergent_regularity.physical_law_status: No particular physical law is derived by this definition.

navigation.coherent_continuation_set: Γ_O(h_n) = {γ | γ begins with h_n and 𝓒(γ | O) = 1}
navigation.interpretation: Navigation is traversal or selection of a continuation within the observer-relative coherent continuation space.
navigation.domain_neutrality_note: Navigation is domain-neutral as a continuation problem. The same formal operator may describe traversal in physical, AI, financial, or other domains once the relevant observer-relative coherence structure has been specified.

geometry.edge_relation: (x,y) ∈ E_O iff x → y is O-coherent
geometry.local_accessible_neighborhood: U_O(x) = {y ∈ 𝓜 | y is reachable from x by an O-coherent path segment}
geometry.interpretation: G_O represents observer-relative relational accessibility among configurations.
geometry.domain_neutrality_note: G_O is a relational graph induced by observer-relative coherence. It may later support domain-specific geometric interpretations, but no physical spacetime identification is assumed at the foundational stage.
geometry.important_constraint: Do not identify G_O with physical spacetime at the foundational stage.

dependency_reference.domain_neutrality_note: This dependency chain is domain-neutral. The same chain applies to physical, AI, financial, and any other domain that can be represented as observer-relative traversal through a static Library. Domains differ only in the interpretation of μ_O and I_N(O), together with the domain-specific meaning assigned to the resulting observer-relative structures.
